propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui multitudinem gentium beati Pauli Apostoli praedicatione docuisti:
da nobis, quaesumus; ut, cujus commemorationem colimus, ejus apud te
patrocinia sentiamus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui
tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 1861 prints one Mass for both Chairs of St Peter. Leaf n546, printed p. 538, heads it `XVIII. St. PETER's CHAIR at ROME, &c.` and rubricates `By omitting the COMM. of St. Prisca +, this Mass serves also for his Chair at Antioch on the 22d February.`, so the 22 February commemoration of St Paul is the `Of St. PAUL` oration printed here. Latin cue `Deus, qui multitudinem.` The Kalendar at leaf n775, printed p. 767, sends 22 February to the same p. 538. A bounded page-image collation confirms the complete target identity. For All Souls this is the first 2-November form only; the second and third forms remain quarantined for substantive wording differences.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: O God, who by the preaching of blessed Paul the Apostle, didst instruct the multitude of the Gentiles: grant, we beseech thee, that whilst we celebrate his memory, we may find the effects of his prayers. Thro'.

tibi tuo grata sunt instituto, gratiora fiant patrocinio supplicantis. Per
Dominum nostrum.

oratio, cujus nos donasti patrocinio gubernari. Per Dominum.
